positions.as_written: Expect the first few degrees of varus to matter more than the next few, since the relationship is not linear.
Assess lateral soft tissue competence, since lateral opening inflates the measured deformity.
Avoid treating mild varus as pathological on its own, because it is common in healthy knees.
Treat the static angle as a surrogate and say so when explaining the rationale for correction.
Address body mass alongside geometry, since both terms sit in the same moment.

Weigh the patient's age, physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and their own ideas, concerns and expectations, because an osteotomy asks a great deal of a patient for a change in a surrogate.
